title: Freelancers or an Agency for Ad Creative? How to Decide
summary: Find out whether bad freelancer ad creative comes from the brief, review or rights, then compare Knowlify and three managed agencies on scope and revisions.
body_markdown:
Often yes, when the problem is the brief, the review and the revisions around the work rather than one weak designer. Knowlify is our top pick if you want finished AI video ads, since a person checks every ad before delivery. Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared. Keep your freelancer if you can supply the brief, a reviewer and the revision budget yourself.


## Diagnose the failure before you switch


Sort the bad work into causes before you pick a replacement. An agency fixes only the causes it can take over, so name the failure in your last three ads first.


What went wrong Likely cause What to change


A wrong product detail or claim reached the ad Nobody checked the ad against approved copy Name a reviewer and give them a claim list


Rewrites never end The brief left out the offer, the audience or the one proof point Write a one-page scope and cap the revisions


You cannot reuse or extend an ad Usage rights and source files were never written down Specify paid and organic usage, duration and source files


Delivery slips No dates or format list were agreed Put dates and specs in the scope


A missed product detail points to review. Endless rewrites point to the brief. If most of the failures sit in the first two rows, an agency with a review step and a written scope can cover them. If they sit in one weak designer's craft, replacing the person may be enough.


Use a written scope as your checklist. NewForm's[full-service page](https://www.newform.com/full-service) says concepts, variations, formats, usage rights and media buying responsibilities are agreed before kickoff, and that media buying is included only when specified for the engagement, as of October 2026. Ask any provider, or your freelancer, to fill in the same list.


AI tools add one more check. Meta's[Ad Creative Generative AI Terms](https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms/ad_creative_generative_ai_terms) make the advertiser solely responsible for checking the accuracy of output from Meta's tools, as of October 2026. The terms cover Meta's own tools, but the same check applies to a freelancer's AI-made scene before it runs. If you are weighing a consultant against a creative shop, our[consultant versus creative agency comparison](https://knowlify.com/articles/facebook-ads-consultant-vs-creative-agency) covers that split.


## How do the options compare?


The options differ mostly in what they take off your plate. Compare what each one includes, who runs the ads and what it costs to publish, rather than the price line alone.


Option What you get Who runs the ads Published price


Knowlify (our top pick) Finished AI video ads, with a person checking every ad Optional end-to-end Meta management, or creative only From $5,000 a month


The UGC Agency Scripts, casting, edits, usage rights and creator payments Your team or agency Not published


Common Thread Collective UGC packages of 20, 40 or 80 ads Creative is sold separately from its Meta ads work No dollar prices on the page


Insense managed UGC 8 video ads per round, creator costs included, 2 revisions Not stated; partnership ads package optional From $3,500 per round, 3-month commitment


## Knowlify: our top pick for finished AI video ads


Knowlify is the best fit when your freelancer problem is that nobody checks the ad before it ships: a person checks every ad before delivery, so the review step you were missing is built in. About 25 finished ads a week arrive in three formats, AI UGC with AI presenters, 3D and character animation, and AI commercials, and the first batch lands on day 5, so you can judge the work early instead of after a month of revisions.


You choose how much to hand over. Take creative only if you have your own media buyer, or have Knowlify run the Meta campaigns end to end. Pricing is a custom quote with no public rate card. The guarantee covers the first 90 days: if the ads have not made more than you paid in that time, you can cancel by email for a full refund ([terms on the site](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. For the AI route, see our[AI UGC ads page](https://knowlify.com/ai-ugc-ads) .


Pick another option when the complaint was about a real person on camera, because Knowlify does not supply real human creators. If the problem was the page the ad sends people to, you need a separate landing page provider, since Knowlify does not build landing pages.


## The UGC Agency and Common Thread Collective: managed creator programs


[The UGC Agency](https://theugc.agency/) says scripts, casting, edits, usage rights and creator payments are all handled, with each stage approved before the next. As of October 2026, its first round of finished ads runs to a 21-day target. It makes the ads but does not run media, so your team or agency runs them.


[Common Thread Collective](https://commonthreadco.com/pages/creative-production) sells UGC in packages of 20 ads from 5 creators, 40 ads from 10 creators and 80 ads from 20 creators, with 3 to 4 weeks per batch. Its page says creator agreements are handled and lists unlimited paid and organic usage rights, as of October 2026. It also makes branded ads from your existing assets, delivered within seven days.
